onboarding.title1: See where the risk is before there is fire
onboarding.text1: Atalaya combines weather, heat spots and fire history into one indicator for each municipality of Nariño. It is a guide, not an exact prediction.
onboarding.text2: Each municipality gets a score from 0 to 100: dry weather (50%), heat spots seen by satellite in the last 5 days (30%) and fires reported before (20%).
onboarding.locationText: Only when you tap “My location” on the map, to show your municipality.
onboarding.internetText: To bring up-to-date weather, heat spots and fire history.
onboarding.text3: Atalaya needs no account. If you don’t allow location, you can search for your municipality on the map.

about.title: About
about.how: The 0–100 score adds three factors: dry weather (50%), nearby heat spots in the last 5 days (30%) and fire history (20%).
about.forecast: The 72 h forecast uses a statistical model (logistic regression) trained on NASA FIRMS heat spots and NASA POWER weather.
about.disclaimer: It is an indicator, not an exact prediction.

how.title: How it works
how.intro: Atalaya brings open data together and sums it up as a risk level for each municipality. This is how it goes from the satellite to the map.
how.flowTitle: From the data to the map
how.step.sourcesText: Heat spots from satellites, weather, recorded fires, recent news and the boundaries of the 64 municipalities.
how.step.ingestText: The server fetches the weather every hour and the heat spots every 3 hours, and at night it reads the fire news, following robots.txt. It keeps 35 days of weather and heat spots.
how.step.scoreText: It adds up three factors of each municipality. Heat spots count within 25 km of the municipal seat, from the last 5 days.
how.step.modelText: A logistic regression model estimates the probability of at least one heat spot within 25 km in the next 72 h, with the forecast weather and the recent heat spots.
how.step.mapText: The map colors each municipality by its level; tap one and its sheet shows the weather, the factors and the forecast.
how.levelsText: The score and the forecast (the probability × 100) use the same cut-offs.
how.not.prediction: It is a risk indicator, not an exact prediction of fires.
how.not.hotspots: The model estimates the probability of heat spots: thermal anomalies seen by the satellite, which can also be farm burning. They are not confirmed fires.
how.not.authorities: It does not replace the authorities. In a fire, follow the instructions of the fire service and disaster risk management.
how.limit.history: Some municipalities have little heat spot history and the model learns mostly from history: it warns little about an extreme event where there were hardly ever heat spots.
how.limit.sources: It depends on its sources: clouds hide heat spots, the satellite passes a few times a day and, if a source fails, the forecast shows the current risk.
how.limit.weather: The model was trained with NASA POWER weather and the app feeds it Open-Meteo, adjusted to the POWER scale; with that adjustment it does a little worse.
how.limit.radius: It counts heat spots in a fixed 25 km radius from the municipal seat, not inside the municipality's boundary.
metrics.title: Model metrics
metrics.predicts: It estimates the probability of at least one heat spot within 25 km of the municipal seat in the next 72 h.
metrics.test: Evaluated on data it never saw: {from} – {to}.
metrics.input: With the adjusted Open-Meteo weather (what the app uses)
metrics.rocAucText: How well it ranks the days with heat spots above the days without them. 0.5 is chance and 1 is perfect.
metrics.prAucText: How right its high probabilities are when heat spots are uncommon. Chance would get the base rate.
metrics.brierText: Mean error of the probability: lower is better.
metrics.brierBaseline: Always predicting the base rate gets {value}.
metrics.baseRate: Base rate: {value} of the evaluated municipality-days had at least one heat spot.
metrics.power: With the NASA POWER weather (the one it was trained with), for comparison:
metrics.factorsTitle: What weighs most in the model
metrics.factorsNote: Weight of each standardized variable. Several are related to each other (rain, humidity), so the sign says how the model uses it, not a cause on its own.
metrics.unavailable: The model metrics are not in this version of the app.
